key_insight: TCP4D uses one shared 4D scene representation to track a robot’s tool-center-point motion and generate future trajectories. Representing actions through the tool center point provides a common motion description across robot embodiments.
problem_solved: Recovering robot actions from RGB video is difficult, particularly when estimating metric 3D tool positions and orientations from monocular observations. The paper also identifies gripper-state annotation as a challenge, though the provided abstract is incomplete.
method: Take a monocular video and initial 2D tool-center-point queries as input.
Use a shared 4D scene representation to recover metric tool-center-point poses, including 3D position and orientation.
Use the same representation to generate future tool-center-point trajectories.
impact: A unified tracking-and-generation model could help practitioners turn robot videos into action data and support motion prediction. Its embodiment-agnostic action representation may also simplify sharing motion descriptions across different robots.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular video + 2D queries → shared 4D representation → tracked poses and future trajectories.
Video frame with a highlighted tool center point and an overlaid 3D coordinate frame.
Trajectory plot showing observed motion as a solid line and generated future motion as a dashed line.
Two different robot arms illustrated with the same tool-center-point action representation.
paper_title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Haosong Peng, Xiangyang Liu, Zhengshen Zhang, Yunfeng Fan, Tianyu Qi
